subject: Discovery recap — Finly (p95 latency, streaming & concurrency)
message_1_subject: Discovery recap — Finly (p95 latency, streaming & concurrency)
message_1_body:
Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, success criteria you mentioned, and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Quick recap of current stack & observed pain:
- Frontend: single-page web chat (React) with streaming token-based updates to improve perceived latency.
- Backend: in-house inference cluster running an open LLM on GPU VMs behind a homegrown router; requests go through a proxy that adds ~20–40ms.
- Current full-request p95 (end-to-end from user input to first streamed tokens) is ~1.1–1.4s under normal load, spikes to ~2.0s during peak.
- Concurrency: production peak ~30 concurrent active users today; expected growth to ~150–200 active concurrent sessions in next 6 months as new product launches.
- Pain: streaming UX stalls (long initial latency), inconsistent p95, and cost-per-request is higher than expected due to lack of batching/kv-cache reuse.

What you told us are the top priorities (success criteria):
- p95 for initial token (stream start) <= 300–400ms end-to-end in our US region for 95% of requests.
- Smooth streaming experience: first token <350ms and subsequent tokens streaming without >100ms jitter.
- Support scale to 150–200 concurrent active users with bounded tail latency and predictable cost.
- Fallback behavior: graceful degradation to smaller models without breaking UX when capacity constrained.

Notes from our side (Redwood implications):
- Serving: we think continuous streaming + early token emission and KV cache reuse will materially reduce observed p95.
- Routing: pinning low-latency GPUs in the same region and using our smart routing can reduce network hops compared to current proxy setup.
- Batching/Caching: short-sequence batching + prefix KV caching for repeated system prompts can cut per-token cost and improve throughput.

Attachments we shared: finly_p95_trace_20270228.pdf (sample traces you shared annotated), mutual_action_plan_finly.xlsx (draft PoC plan & milestones).

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll run a short benchmark (Redwood-managed) against a representative prompt set you provided. Goal: measure p95 and streaming start latency at 30, 75, and 150 concurrent sessions.
2) PoC: 2-week pilot with dedicated capacity & observability (detailed MAP in attached xlsx).
3) Sync: schedule 30–45 min bench review next week to go over initial results and iterate on config.

Can you confirm: (a) the token limits we should test (you mentioned 512 typical length), and (b) whether the test traffic can be routed from a US-West region? Also confirm calendar windows that work for a bench review next week.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate schedules once you confirm.

Best,
Aditya
Aditya Rao

message_2_subject: Re: Discovery recap — Finly (p95 latency, streaming & concurrency)
message_2_body:
Thanks Aditya — solid recap and exactly what we discussed. A few clarifications: 

- Token lengths: 512 is our typical median; 1024 is the 95th percentile we care about for long queries. Please include both in the benchmark.
- Region: yes, start from US-West (we have most traffic there).
- Peak concurrency: to be clear, 150 is our near-term target and 200 is our design target. Please scale tests accordingly.

We’re OK with the proposed bench and the 2-week PoC.

For the bench review, Wednesday 2027-03-03 between 10:00–11:00 PT works for me. Bob will join as well.

FYI — attaching one more trace from a production peak this month (I’ll upload to the Drive folder you linked).

- Test types: cold-start, warm (KV cache primed), and streaming latency under sustained load.
- Deliverable: bench report + recommendations (model variant, quantization, batching settings) within 3 business days after the bench run.

We’ll schedule the bench for Tuesday 2027-03-02 evening (we’ll run the tests when your traffic is low) and share results by end of day Thursday 2027-03-04 so we can review on the Wed window you suggested if needed.

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Best,
Aditya
